CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to reassess the management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, and to evaluate the effectiveness of the recent medication adjustments.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, expressing mixed feelings about his current treatment regimen. He reports that while his anxiety levels remain stable, he continues to experience significant irritability and concentration difficulties, which have been exacerbated by increased work-related stress. He has adhered to the sertraline regimen of 300 mg daily, but he notes that his mood fluctuations have not improved as hoped.
His tension-type headaches have decreased in frequency to two times a week, with an average intensity rating of 4 out of 10. He reports that the increase in topiramate to 150 mg daily has been beneficial, allowing him to reduce his reliance on ibuprofen, which he now uses less frequently. However, he remains cautious about overuse due to his history of gastrointestinal issues.
Sleep quality has shown marginal improvement, with Mr. Smith averaging 7 to 8 hours of sleep per night. However, he still experiences difficulty initiating sleep on some nights, which he attributes to residual anxiety. He continues to take trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime and has found it somewhat effective, but he remains concerned about the lingering drowsiness from gabapentin, which he continues to take at 200 mg nightly.
Despite these improvements, persistent fatigue remains a significant barrier to his daily functioning, particularly in the afternoons. Mr. Smith describes episodes of exhaustion that disrupt his productivity, prompting him to consider further modifications to his work schedule and lifestyle.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 150 mg daily (increased) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 9. Gabapentin 200 mg at bedtime (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to engage in physical activity, maintaining his lunchtime walks at 30 minutes and incorporating weekend hikes. He reports adherence to a balanced diet and has successfully limited caffeine intake. He has begun exploring mindfulness techniques, including meditation, which he finds helpful in managing his anxiety. He expresses interest in attending a yoga class to further enhance his relaxation practices.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; mild irritability persists; sleep quality slightly improved; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Headache frequency decreased; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue noted, particularly in the afternoons, with no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/74 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.4F - General: Alert, oriented; appears more rested than previous visit; mood appears anxious but engaged. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; tenderness noted in the bilateral temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with mild distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Consider referral for cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to address ongoing symptoms and coping strategies. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime; reassess efficacy and side effects in one month. Gabapentin at 200 mg may be maintained, with close monitoring for residual drowsiness. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; monitor headache diary for further reduction in frequency and intensity. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Recommend continued lifestyle modifications, including regular physical activity and stress management techniques. Explore additional support through occupational therapy if fatigue persists.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-12-29 to evaluate symptom progression, medication efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain an open dialogue regarding his treatment response and any lifestyle changes he implements.
